findings.title: updateMany with an empty data object cannot bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty data object to Prisma `updateMany`. Prisma rejects empty update data or produces no real update, so it will not update `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` as the comment claims, and it may throw. This runs after availability cache is written in `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, so a throw here can fail the Google webhook/cache-refresh path after cache was already updated. Pass a concrete field such as `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` if the timestamp bump is intended, or remove the call if it is not needed.

findings.title: deleteCache success does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation only calls `onSuccess?.()` and shows a toast. It does not invalidate `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates that query in `onSettled`. As a result, after deleting cached data the `cacheUpdatedAt` already loaded in the UI remains stale, so the cache status and delete action are still shown until a manual refetch. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in the delete mutation's success or settled handler.

findings.title: Cache status query includes expired calendar cache entries
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all CalendarCache rows for the given credential IDs without filtering on `expiresAt`. The actual cache lookup in `getCachedAvailability` only uses rows where `expiresAt >= now()`, so the new UI can report that cache exists for a credential whose cached entries are expired and would not be served. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause so the status matches effective cache data.

findings.title: Passing optional/null cacheUpdatedAt to Date constructor is not type-safe
findings.body: `cacheUpdatedAt` is declared as `Date | null | undefined`, but `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` is called after only checking the separate `hasCache` boolean. TypeScript does not narrow `cacheUpdatedAt` through an aliased boolean check, so with strict null checks this is a compile error; the code is also not type-safe as written. Use a narrowed local value after checking `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` directly, or pass a non-null assertion/cast, before constructing the Date.
